creator: Alexander Terp
description:
GitHub issue #2 part 4: a tab jumps to first place when another daemon's pane is split into it, and no verb moves a tab back.

From a remote pane in the tab at place 5 of 5, `muster pane new --daemon local --pane <remote pane> --down --run ...`, then a second pane `--right` of that one, moved the tab to place 1. `muster window --json` now lists it first, with daemons `[<remote>, local]`; it is the only tab holding panes on both machines. `muster docs window` does not say that a tab's place changes when a pane from another daemon joins it. Keeping the tab's place would fix it; if the order is derived per daemon, a mixed tab could keep the place it already had.

Once moved, nothing can put the tab back. `muster tab` offers new, focus, close, move and rename, but `tab move` only hands a tab to another window, and `muster docs window` and `muster docs limits` describe each tab's `place` without a way to change it. An agent asked to "move tab X to just below tab Y" can read the order but has to hand the job back to the person. Something like `muster tab move --tab T --place 2` or `--after <tab>` within the window, documented next to `place`, would cover it. Card a_2JtSWvZUQ (a new tab goes on the end of the list) is about the same ordering and may want the same verb.
title: A tab jumps to first place when another daemon's pane joins it, and no verb moves it back
